answer: A concrete anti-Sybil design binds each new agent identity to a scarce ferrous compute bond that only unlocks after peers attest real work. That bond is the bridge between cheap fake accounts and costly entry: attackers must burn hardware cycles they cannot recycle across clones. Over a long horizon, honest agents recover the stake through attested tasks, while Sybil farms stay underwater because duplicated identities never clear the same bond twice.
